literature_notes: All four ledger clips (L1–L4) describe GFP-tagged full-length MSLN constructs expressed in HEK293T cells with confirmed surface display. However, none qualifies as a pinnable site under the stated rules. L1 (PMC10303918) cites a SinoBiologicals 'C-GFPSpark' commercial plasmid: the 'C-' prefix indicates a C-terminal tag, but the exact residue junction is not stated anywhere in the clip, and the rules explicitly disqualify 'a commercial plasmid whose tag POSITION is unstated; you cannot pin insert_after_residue.' L2–L4 (PMC13158456) all describe the same 'GFP-tagged human MSLN expression vector' used for biopanning; they name neither a residue nor even whether the tag is N- or C-terminal. The topology_derived rule ('exactly ONE terminus is extracellular') cannot rescue these clips: per the given landmarks, MSLN has EXTRACELLULAR: 37–630 with no TM domain, so both the mature N-terminus (residue 37, after signal-peptide cleavage at 36/37) and the C-terminus (residue 630) are extracellular — two extracellular termini, not one. Even if L1's 'C-terminal' label were used to narrow to the C-terminus, the GPI-signal region (approximately residues 581–630, cleaved post-translationally) makes the exact surface-exposed C-terminal junction ambiguous and not derivable from the topology landmarks alone. Because no clip names a residue, no clip is a non-commercial source with a single extracellular terminus, and the commercial-plasmid disqualification applies to L1, zero sites are reported. This is the correct answer given the ledger.
